notes: Fixtures under fixtures/<repo>/ are placed at the work repo root. Every assertion a program can decide is graded by checks.py; the rest go to the model grader.

evals.name: greenfield-node
evals.prompt: I have a Node.js Express app in this repo (package.json with an Express dependency, app entrypoint at src/server.js, listens on port 3000). There are no Docker files yet. Please containerize it so I can build and ship it.
evals.expected_output: A modern multi-stage Dockerfile with the syntax frontend line first, version ARGs at top, hardened base images pinned by digest, a .dockerignore derived from .gitignore plus Docker additions, a docker-bake.hcl, and the assistant asking whether to also add a compose.yaml since this is first-time Docker setup.
expectations: The Dockerfile's first line is exactly `# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1`.
The Dockerfile declares at least one `ARG` before its first `FROM`, and every `FROM` that names an external image ends with `AS <name>`.
The final stage is built on a hardened image (following stage aliases): `cgr.dev/chainguard/` or `dhi.io/`.
Every `FROM` that names an external image carries `@sha256:` followed by 64 hex characters, or a `@sha256:` placeholder with the answer naming `regctl` or `docker buildx imagetools` to resolve it.
A `.dockerignore` exists with a `.git` entry and the `coverage/` entry copied from the repo's `.gitignore`.
A `docker-bake.hcl` exists with a `target` block that sets `dockerfile` and `tags`.
No `compose.yaml` was created, and the answer asks or offers to add one rather than deciding silently.
The final stage's `ENTRYPOINT` or `CMD` is in exec form (a JSON array).
The hand-back gives a one-line reason for each opinionated default it applied (frontend pin, hardened base, digest pin, .dockerignore, bake file).

evals.name: go-distroless
evals.prompt: Write me a Dockerfile for a Go microservice. The module builds with `go build ./cmd/api` and the binary serves HTTP on 8080. I want the smallest, most secure production image you can reasonably make.
evals.expected_output: A multi-stage Dockerfile using a Chainguard go -dev (or DHI) build stage and a distroless static final stage, with the syntax line first, version ARGs, digest pins, BuildKit cache mounts for the Go build, CGO disabled, and an exec-form ENTRYPOINT.
expectations: The Dockerfile's first line is exactly `# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1`.
The final stage is built on a static or distroless image (following stage aliases): its image name contains `static` or `distroless`.
The Dockerfile declares at least one `ARG` before its first `FROM`, and every `FROM` that names an external image ends with `AS <name>`.
A `RUN` that runs `go build` or `go mod download` uses `--mount=type=cache`.
Every `FROM` that names an external image carries `@sha256:` followed by 64 hex characters, or a `@sha256:` placeholder with the answer naming `regctl` or `docker buildx imagetools` to resolve it.
The final stage's `ENTRYPOINT` or `CMD` is in exec form (a JSON array).
The build sets `CGO_ENABLED=0`.
A `.dockerignore` and a `docker-bake.hcl` are created.

evals.name: modernize-legacy
evals.prompt: Modernize my Docker setup. My Dockerfile starts with `FROM node:18` and has no syntax line. My docker-compose.yml has `version: "3.8"` at the top and uses a bind mount `- ./src:/app/src` for live code reloading during development. Please bring these up to current best practices.
evals.expected_output: An updated Dockerfile with the frontend directive, a supported Node version pinned by digest, and modern structure, plus the compose file renamed to compose.yaml with the obsolete version key removed and the dev bind mount replaced by a develop.watch sync configuration.
expectations: The updated Dockerfile's first line is exactly `# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1`.
The compose file in the output has no top-level `version:` key.
The output compose file is named `compose.yaml`.
The compose file has a `develop.watch` entry with `action: sync` for the source path, and no `./src:/app/src` volume.
The answer names `docker compose watch` (or `docker compose up --watch`) as the run command.
No `FROM` line still uses `node:18`, and every external `FROM` carries `@sha256:` followed by 64 hex characters or a `@sha256:` placeholder with a resolve command.
A `.dockerignore` is created.
The answer explains why each modernization matters, one reason per change.
